channel.title: Homeworld Press
channel.description: Independent editorial coverage of sci-fi literature, technology, space science, and tested buyer's guides.

item.title: Three Helicopters Underwrite NASA's Reactor Demonstration
item.description: SkyFall flies on a nuclear carrier that may not be ready, and its own project scientist says a Falcon 9 would do.

item.title: Contact Theory Meets the Feed and Brings Fine Print
item.description: A November 2026 report on Instagram-mediated intergroup contact puts its concession in the headline. The order of those clauses is the most useful thing the study has to say.

item.title: Moon Bricks Have to Hold Air, Not Weight
item.description: Interlocking regolith brick is a shielding story rather than a pressure shell, and the figure worth demanding is a cycle count.

item.title: A Lunar Land Office Has to Open Before the Claims Do
item.description: Space.com's frontier warning reads better as an argument about survey data, reference frames and who gets to file first.

item.title: A New Ocean Vehicle Class Has to Sacrifice One Constraint
item.description: The November 20 item on Deep Venture uses the word class without the specification that would defend it. Every such claim has one testable tell.

item.title: Eufy's Omni C28 Needs a Baseline Before 53 Percent Means Anything
item.description: The reported figure is a ratio and not a price. Without the starting price, the parts cost and the retailer, a buyer cannot convert it into a decision.

item.title: Open Ocean Forecasts Will Decide the Navy's Next Weather Model
item.description: A report says NEPTUNE is poised to take over the Navy's global weather model, with gains over open ocean. The record behind that promise is one sentence, and the sentence is the weak part.

item.title: Apple's Neuromancer Must Invent the Plot the Novel Never Carried
item.description: The promotion leads with a calendar and a cast list. The hard part is that the book is famous for its sentences, not its story.

item.title: Euclid's First Comet Tests the Boring Half of a Cosmology Camera
item.description: What the detection proves first is the data pipeline; the object itself is where the announcement runs out.

item.title: Voyager 1 launched second and outran Voyager 2 to a light-day
item.description: Each trajectory was handed a different amount of speed before launch, depending on which planets it was pointed at.
